q: Which word tells about the TEXTURE of a cotton ball?
e: Texture is how something feels. A cotton ball feels soft.

q: Which material is a brick for building a wall made of?
e: Material is what an object is made of. A brick is made of baked clay.

q: You sort blocks into two groups: RED and BLUE. What property did you use?
e: Sorting into red and blue groups uses color.

q: Which object is made of metal?
e: A spoon is usually made of metal. The others are paper, wool, and wood.

q: Which two objects have the same SHAPE?
e: A ball and an orange are both round like a sphere.

q: A sandpaper sheet feels rough. A glass window feels smooth. What property is different?
e: Rough and smooth tell how things feel, which is texture.

q: Which group could hold ONLY things made of wood?
o: a spoon, a coin, a key
a sock, a hat, a scarf
a pencil, a chair, a block
a bottle, a cup, a bowl made of plastic
e: A pencil, a chair, and a block can all be made of wood.

q: Which object will a magnet pull toward it?
e: Magnets pull some metals, like iron. A paper clip is made of steel.

q: Which object will a magnet NOT pick up?
e: Magnets do not pull plastic.

q: A magnet moves a toy car closer to it. What did the magnet do?
e: Moving the car closer means the magnet pulled it.

q: Two magnets are put together and move AWAY from each other. What happened?
e: Magnets can push each other away.

q: A magnet can make some things move without touching them. What does a magnet do?
e: A magnet pushes or pulls some objects.

q: You predict a magnet will pick up a coin made of wood. Is it a good prediction?
o: no, wood is not pulled by a magnet
yes, magnets pick up all things
e: Magnets do not pull wood.

q: Which tool could a magnet help you use to pick up pins spilled on the floor?
e: Steel pins are pulled to a magnet.

q: What do you need in order to see objects?
e: Objects can only be seen when there is light.

q: A closet has no light and the door is shut. What can you see inside?
e: Without a light source, objects cannot be seen.

q: Which is a source of light?
e: The Sun makes its own light. The Moon and a mirror only reflect light.

q: Which room is the BRIGHTEST?
o: a room with the curtains closed and no lights
a room with the lamp on and the window open
a room with only a small night-light
a room with the lights off
e: More light makes things look brighter.

q: It is dim in a room. What can you do to see a book better?
e: A lamp adds light so the book is easier to see.

q: Which object makes its own light?
e: A flashlight makes light. The others do not.

q: Two pictures are on a wall. One is in bright light and one is in dim light. Which is easier to see?
e: More light makes objects easier to see.

q: Light goes through a clear window. What does the window do to light?
e: Clear glass lets light pass through.

q: What makes a shadow?
e: A shadow forms when an object blocks light.

q: Which object makes the DARKEST shadow?
e: A wooden board blocks light. Clear things let light through.

q: Where do you see your shadow on a sunny day?
o: on the ground away from the Sun
e: Your body blocks sunlight, so a shadow forms on the ground.

q: Which object lets MOST light pass through?
e: A clear glass jar lets light through.

q: A student holds a hand in front of a flashlight. What appears on the wall?
e: The hand blocks the light and makes a shadow.

q: Which object blocks light, so it makes a shadow?
e: A book blocks light. The other choices are clear.

q: When is the Sun seen in the sky?
e: We see the Sun during the day.

q: What comes after day?
e: Night follows day.

q: Which is something you can see in the sky at night?
e: Stars are seen at night. The Sun is seen during the day.

q: When do most people sleep?
o: at noon when it is bright
at night when it is dark
e: Most people sleep at night when it is dark.

q: Is it warmer outside in the middle of a sunny day or in the middle of the night?
o: in the middle of the day
in the middle of the night
it is warmer at night in every season
e: The Sun warms the Earth during the day.

q: The pattern of day and night happens over and over. Which comes first, then second?
e: Day and night take turns in a repeating pattern.

q: A student sees the Sun coming up in the morning. What will happen later that day?
o: the Sun will stay up all night
the stars will come out first
the Sun will go down and it will get dark
the Moon will stay out all day
e: After the Sun sets, it gets dark and night begins.

q: Which object in the sky gives us light and heat during the day?
e: The Sun gives light and heat to Earth.

q: Which of these can you see in the sky during the day?
e: Clouds are seen in the sky during the day.

q: Which sky object do people often see at night with a different shape on different nights?
e: The Moon looks different on different nights.

q: Which sky objects look like tiny dots of light at night?
e: Stars look like tiny dots of light at night.

q: Which sky object is white and fluffy?
e: Many clouds look white and fluffy.

q: A student draws the sky at night. Which picture shows a night sky?
o: a bright blue sky with the Sun
e: Moon and stars are seen at night.

q: Which sky object is closest to Earth?
e: The Moon is the closest object of these to Earth.

q: Which rock is the BIGGEST?
o: a boulder as big as a car
e: A boulder is the biggest of these rocks. A grain of sand is the smallest.

q: Which word describes the SHAPE of a rock that looks like a ball?
e: A ball shape is round. It has no flat sides or corners.

q: Two rocks are the same size and shape. One is red and one is gray. What is different?
e: The rocks match in size and shape. Only the color is different.

q: Which rock feels SMOOTH when you touch it?
o: a rough rock with many bumps
a river stone worn down by water
a broken rock with jagged edges
a rock with many sharp points
e: Water wears rocks smooth over time. Sharp, bumpy, and jagged rocks feel rough.

q: A student sorts rocks into a SMOOTH group and a ROUGH group. Which rock goes in the SMOOTH group?
o: a rock with pits and bumps
a rock with sharp broken edges
a rock with a shiny, polished surface
a rock covered in tiny grains
e: A shiny, polished rock feels smooth. The other three feel rough.

q: Which rock has a FLAT shape, like a pancake?
e: A slab is flat. A ball is round, and a cone and a stick are not flat.

q: Which list puts rocks in order from SMALLEST to BIGGEST?
o: a grain of sand, a pebble, a boulder
a boulder, a grain of sand, a pebble
a boulder, a pebble, a grain of sand
a pebble, a boulder, a grain of sand
e: A grain of sand is the smallest, then a pebble, then a boulder.

q: Which is a kind of weather?
e: Rainy tells what the weather is like.

q: Which season is usually the coldest?
e: Winter is usually the coldest season.

q: Which season usually has the hottest days?
e: Summer usually has the hottest days.

q: Monday was sunny. Tuesday was rainy. What does this show?
o: weather can change from day to day
it is always sunny on Monday
e: Weather can be different from one day to the next.

q: Leaves change color and drop off many trees, and the days get cooler. Which season is it?
e: Falling leaves and cooler days are signs of fall.

q: What should you wear outside on a very cold, snowy day?
e: A warm coat keeps you warm in cold weather.

q: A thermometer shows how hot or cold the air is. What does it tell about?
e: A thermometer measures temperature.

q: What is wind?
e: Wind is air that is moving.

q: A pinwheel spins when you blow on it. What makes it spin?
e: Moving air pushes the pinwheel.

q: A balloon gets bigger when you blow into it. What is inside?
e: Air fills the balloon and makes it bigger.

q: Which shows that wind is blowing?
o: a pencil is on the floor
a book lies on a desk
e: A waving flag shows moving air.

q: Where is air found?
e: Air is all around us even though we cannot see it.

q: Which tool shows which way the wind blows?
e: A windsock points the way the wind is blowing.

q: A kite flies high on a day with strong wind. Why?
o: the kite makes its own light
e: Moving air pushes against the kite and lifts it.

q: What do plants need from soil?
o: nutrients and a place to grow
e: Plants get nutrients and a place to grow from soil.

q: Which is a way people use water?
e: People drink water to stay healthy.

q: How can people use rocks?
e: People use rocks to build walls, roads, and houses.

q: Which use of water is for staying clean?
e: Washing hands uses water to get clean.

q: A farmer grows food in the ground. What material is used?
e: Farmers grow food in soil.

q: Which job needs water?
e: A garden needs water to grow.

q: Which is a way to use sand and rocks?
e: People use sand and rocks to make paths and roads.

q: What do plants need to grow?
e: Plants need water, sunlight, air, nutrients, and space.

q: A plant sits in a dark closet and is never watered. What will happen?
o: it will turn into an animal
e: Plants need light and water to grow well.

q: Where do plants get nutrients?
e: Plant roots take in nutrients from the soil.

q: Why do many plants grow toward a window?
e: Plants grow toward light because they need sunlight.

q: Seeds are planted too close together. What might the plants be missing?
e: Plants need space to grow.

q: Which is NOT needed for a plant to live?
e: Plants need air, water, and sunlight, but not toys.

q: A student gives one plant water and sun and another plant only sun. Which plant will grow better?
o: the plant with water and sun
e: Plants need both water and sunlight.

q: What do animals need to live?
e: Animals need air, water, food, space, and shelter.

q: A bird builds a nest. What does the nest give the bird?
e: A nest is a shelter for the bird.

q: A fish lives in water. What does water give the fish?
o: a place to nap on a bed
a place to live and the air it needs
e: Fish live in water and take in air from it.

q: A rabbit eats grass. What does grass give the rabbit?
e: The rabbit gets food from grass.

q: A dog needs room to run and play. What is this need called?
e: Animals need space to move and live.

q: A squirrel hides in a hole in a tree during a storm. What does the hole give the squirrel?
e: A hole in a tree is a shelter.

q: A pet has food, shelter, and space but no water. What will happen?
o: it will be fine for a year
it will turn into a plant
e: Animals need water to live.

q: Which part of a plant grows under the ground?
e: Roots grow under the ground.

q: Which plant part holds the plant up?
e: The stem holds up the plant.

q: Which plant part makes food using sunlight?
e: Leaves use sunlight to make food for the plant.

q: Which plant part is often colorful and smells nice?
e: Flowers are often colorful and smell nice.

q: Which plant part takes in water from the soil?
e: Roots take in water from the soil.

q: An apple is the part of an apple tree that holds the seeds. What is it called?
e: A fruit holds the seeds.

q: Which list names only plant parts?
e: Roots, stems, and leaves are parts of a plant.

q: Which body part helps a person see?
e: Eyes are used for seeing.

q: Which body part helps an animal hear?
e: Ears are used for hearing.

q: A bird uses its wings to do what?
e: Wings help birds fly.

q: A monkey uses its hands and tail to do what?
e: Monkeys grasp branches with hands and tail.

q: A fish uses its fins to do what?
e: Fins help fish move in water.

q: A dog sniffs the air. Which body part is it using?
e: A dog smells with its nose.

q: Which animal body part helps it grab food?
e: A bird uses its claws to grab food.

q: What comes first in a plant life cycle?
e: A plant life cycle starts with a seed.

q: A seed begins to grow and a tiny plant comes out. What is it called?
e: A tiny new plant is a seedling.

q: Which shows the plant life cycle in order?
e: A plant grows from seed to seedling to plant, then makes flowers and fruit.

q: What do flowers on a plant often turn into?
e: Flowers can become fruit with seeds inside.

q: A seedling grows bigger. What does it become?
e: A seedling grows into a plant.

q: What is inside many fruits?
e: Many fruits have seeds inside.

q: A student draws four pictures of a bean plant. Which picture should come SECOND?
e: The seed comes first, then the seedling.

q: A seed is taken from a parent plant and planted. What will the seed grow into?
o: a plant of a very different kind
a young plant that looks like the parent
e: Seeds grow into the same kind of plant as the parent.

q: A bean seed is planted. What will grow?
e: A bean seed grows into a bean plant.

q: A young oak tree looks most like which plant?
e: Young plants look like their parent plants.

q: A seedling has leaves that look like its parent's leaves. What does this show?
o: young plants look like their parents
e: Young plants resemble their parent plants.

q: Which seed would grow into a plant with many yellow petals like its parent?
o: a seed from a pine tree
e: A sunflower seed grows into a sunflower.

q: A tomato seed is planted. What will grow?
e: Seeds grow into the same kind of plant.

q: A grown pine tree makes seeds. What will a pine seed grow into?
e: A pine seed grows into a pine tree.
